title: BeanCounter: A low-toxicity, large-scale, and open dataset of business-oriented text
benchmark_measurement: Prevalence of religious demographic descriptors (e.g., 'Christian', 'Jewish') and the average toxicity score of sentences containing these descriptors, comparing the custom 'BeanCounter' dataset to the 'C4-en' dataset.
findings: The BeanCounter dataset has a significant representation of religious content (9.52% of filings), skewed towards Western identities like 'Christian'. The context surrounding religious descriptors is 66-87% less toxic compared to the web-crawled C4-en dataset. For example, sentences containing the term 'Christian' are 87.48% less toxic on average. Models continually pre-trained on BeanCounter showed improved safety scores (reduced toxic generation propensity) for groups like 'jewish' and 'muslim'.
